title: Publish canonical and social preview metadata from the existing Astro page and hosted product evidence

scope.subject: Use Astro's native site/url primitives and standard HTML metadata to publish canonical, Open Graph and Twitter/X preview tags for the single public Personal Universe page, reusing an already-hosted Galaxy acceptance screenshot as the preview image instead of adding an SEO runtime or promotional rendering system

research_summary: The public Pages deployment has a stable Astro site/base configuration but index.astro currently exposes only a title, theme color and implementation-oriented description. Astro's official documentation recommends standard HTML head metadata and provides Astro.site/Astro.url for canonical and absolute social URLs. The Open Graph protocol needs title/type/image/url plus a concise description for a useful rich preview. Mature Astro SEO components exist, but this product has one static page and fixed metadata, so adding an SEO package would create dependency/configuration surface without replacing any missing domain logic. Reuse the existing hosted desktop Galaxy screenshot as the social image; Playwright already produces the accepted product frame in the same cloud environment used for release validation.

sources.finding: Astro's site option is the final deployed URL and base is the deployment path, so the existing PUBLIC_SITE_URL/PUBLIC_BASE_PATH configuration already supplies the production URL authority.
Astro.url and Astro.site are documented primitives for constructing canonical URLs and absolute social-image URLs directly in a page.
Astro explicitly recommends adding common SEO/site metadata with standard HTML link/meta tags in the page head rather than configuration.
The Open Graph protocol defines og:title, og:type, og:image and og:url as basic metadata, with og:description and image alt as useful additions.
astro-seo is a mature MIT component for canonical/Open Graph metadata, but using it here would add a package abstraction for one fixed static page whose tags Astro can render natively.
Playwright can capture page screenshots as image buffers/files; the project already preserves hosted Galaxy screenshots as release artifacts suitable for reuse as a truthful product preview.

search_ladder.conclusion: A full Astro SEO component can render all required tags, but it is disproportionate for a single static route with fixed metadata and would add dependency/configuration surface without improving correctness.
Reuse Astro's configured site/base plus Astro.site/Astro.url and ordinary head tags as the metadata authority.
No sitemap, CMS SEO subsystem or JSON-LD graph is required to close the current single-page canonical/social-preview gap.
Reuse the already-accepted hosted desktop Galaxy frame as a static social preview asset, and use the existing browser suite to validate emitted metadata and asset reachability.

candidates.name: astro-seo component
candidates.reason: Provides broad SEO abstractions but this site has one fixed page and the required tags are directly supported by Astro/native HTML; adding a dependency creates more maintenance and upgrade surface than capability.

candidates.name: Astro site/url plus native head metadata
candidates.source: Existing Astro page/configuration and standard HTML metadata
candidates.reason: Closes the exact canonical/Open Graph/Twitter gap with no new runtime or dependency and automatically respects the configured production site/base path.

candidates.name: Existing hosted Galaxy acceptance screenshot
candidates.source: Protected hosted visual acceptance artifact from the current Personal Universe product
candidates.license: project-owned product output / Apache-2.0 test tooling
candidates.reason: Uses a truthful, already-accepted product frame rather than creating a separate marketing illustration that can drift from the actual experience.

decision.rationale: Use the framework capabilities already present in Astro for URL construction and native head tags, and reuse a current hosted product screenshot for the preview image. This yields canonical and social previews without a new SEO dependency or separate promotional renderer.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: The full SEO component is broader, but this project currently has one static public route and fixed page metadata. Native Astro/HTML covers the entire required gap with fewer dependencies, no component-specific API to maintain, and direct alignment with Astro's own recommendation to place common metadata in the page head.

decision.fallback: If the site later grows multiple route-specific SEO schemas or structured-data graphs, reassess a reusable SEO component then; do not introduce it for the current one-page metadata gap.
